card.name: Verb right after may in warnings
card.fires_on: The word right after "may" (or a similar hedge like "is expected") in drug-warning sentences, such as "may become elevated" or "may be attenuated". It is weaker on linking words like "that" or "which" that begin a clause about an effect.

modes.label: After may
modes.description: "become" or "be" right after "may" before a change in effect or pressure.
modes.example: Intraocular pressure may<< become>> elevated in some patients taking corticoster

modes.label: Expected or linking word
modes.description: "expected", "that" or "which" introducing a predicted effect or follow-up clause.
modes.example: is<< expected>> to decrease the concentration of ledipas

card.plain: It fires on the small word after "may" in warnings, just before the sentence says what changes.
